sources.title: Eva Myrdal, Iron, Honey and Wild Cinnamon: Forest Resource Extraction in Sri Lanka’s Historical Landscape (2025)
sources.note: Original full indexed paper, section on Sihigiri Bim epigraphy and notes34 to 35: mid-ninth to tenth-century inscriptions, competing royal/monastic rights in water, land, labour and produce. Earlier iron furnaces and1990s honey gathering not projected into ninth century.

sources.title: Siddham IN03143, Kivulekada Pillar Inscription of Sena I
sources.note: Direct scholarly corpus description. Ninth-century SenaI attribution from Salamevan title and Ritigala foundation. Date assigned after Pandyan raid; competing absolute reign dates not harmonized artificially. Discovery1892 granary support and1928 rediscovery. Edition/translation subpages unavailable; text sample separately verified in Sundberg.

sources.title: Siddham IN03193, Viyaulpata Pillar Inscription
sources.note: Direct corpus: first regnal year of SenaII, mahapaMahinda, monastic grant, two named officers, assembled notables and public proclamation. Reign-start alternatives846/866 differ from commonly used853; public copy uses ninth century.

sources.title: Wijerathne Bohingamuwa, Military Role of Mahatittha: A Historical Reappraisal (2014), pp. 101 to 104
sources.note: Direct four-page proceedings paper. Printed102 SenaII expedition from Mantai; printed103 explicitly warns chronicles privilege warfare and require archaeology for economic history. Author incorrect/variant reign-start833 omitted.

sources.title: Robin Coningham and colleagues, From village to state, and back again (published online 2026)
sources.note: Full indexed original, World Archaeology57(1),26 to 45; direct publisher access403 and PMCcaptcha. Printed30 ASW2 early-medieval residential ceramics/nambiliya rice-processing interpretation; introduction reservoirs; later change not sudden total disappearance. 2025volume label but online1May2026.

sources.title: Eleanor Kingwell-Banham and colleagues, Spice and rice at ancient Mantai (2018)
sources.note: Full indexed original archaeobotanical report; direct page429. Figure5 ninth-century Changsha ceramics; plant-foods section rice/wheat/pulses and palm phytoliths. Multi-period2009 to 2010 assemblage explicitly scoped. Phase3AD850 to 1400 mixed/disturbed; avoid clove900 to 1100 as secure ninth-century event. No total assemblage percentage projected into one century.

sources.title: Sasni Amarasekara, Buddhist Meditation Monasteries in Ancient Sri Lanka (2017), pp. 59 to 68
sources.note: Direct ten-page research paper examining surviving structures. Printed64 double platforms,65 walkways/hot-waterbath,65 to 66 urinal/latrine types. Motive for decoration remains debated. No uncritical claim six rooms proves six occupants or that these are royal palaces.

sources.title: Sumudu Dharmarathna, Mahayana-Tantrayana Traditions and Transition of Monastic Architecture in Ancient Sri Lanka (2022)
sources.note: Direct journal issue, article1, printed18 to 19: ninth-century Mihintale hospital identified through inscription and material remains; body-shaped bath, court-facing cells, outer refectory and medicine preparation/storage. Later Polonnaruwa toilets and baths not borrowed into Mihintale.

sources.title: Jeffrey R. Sundberg, Abhayagirivihara’s Pamsukulika Monks, Pacific World 16 (2014), p. 119
sources.note: Indexed original printed119 note17 gives exact Riṭgal-aram kärū Salamevan Rajpahi and identifies founder ofRitigala; cites Ranawella InscriptionsofCeylon5(1):1 to 12. DirectPDFfailed. Query exactURLplusSalamevan119 reproduces. Use scholarly Latin-letter transcription; no unverified Sinhala glyphs. Conservatively budget with SiddhamKivulekada as underlying same inscription.

sources.title: Nimal de Silva, Sigiriya Mirror Wall and the Graffiti, National Trust Sri Lanka lecture (2012)
sources.note: Original indexed PDF printed24 graffiti corpus/scholars; printed25 Budalmi, transcription and English gloss. DirectPDFfailed for both2018and2022copies. Short sample uses verifiedLatintranscription; no individual ninth-century date established. Corpus extends sixth to thirteenth centuries; text explicitly broader medieval context. Lecture37inNationalTrust2012programme confirmsauthor/date.

sources.title: UNESCO, Ancient City of Polonnaruwa
sources.note: Direct description: destruction of Anuradhapura993, successorcapital and survivingChola/Parakramabahu monuments. ReadwithBohingamuwa onCholaoccupation; notinstanttotalpopulationdisappearance.
